data.cases: random (seeds 0-2, N up to 131072), special grid incl. extrema/subnormals/signed zeros, cancellation-biased, extreme ratio, storage-offset views, shared storage
data.expected_signal: componentwise tolerance violations on adversarial FP16 domain

evidence.summary: Full adversarial sweep (random N up to 131072, special-value grid with extrema/subnormals/signed zeros, cancellation-biased near-parallel numerators, extreme magnitude ratios up to 65504/6e-8, contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets, shared backing storage) compared kernel.run output to FP64 reference componentwise under tol 1e-7+5e-7|target|: 0 of 1,228,740 components violated tolerance, all outputs finite, and inputs were preserved. The FP32 intermediate precision is sufficient over the tested legal domain.

rationale: The kernel converts FP16 components to FP32, computes products/sums and a round-to-nearest division. Products of two FP16 values are exact in FP32 (≤22 significand bits), so each component's relative error should stay under ~3e-7, within the contract tolerance of 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| even for near-cancelling small components.

scope_evidence.summary: abs(actual - target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7 * abs(target), componentwise, and 'EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals and both extrema.'

scope_rationale: The contract requires componentwise accuracy abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| for every finite FP16 combination including extrema, subnormals, and near-cancellation cases, so any such input failing tolerance is a contract violation.
statement: The kernel's FP32 intermediate computation fails the componentwise tolerance on some legal FP16 inputs (e.g., catastrophic cancellation in a*c+b*d, or extrema magnitudes).
